record.paper_title: Major Unsolved Problems in Space Plasma Physics
record.original_question: Why do outward-propagating Alfvenic fluctuations in the solar wind evolve and disappear in the outer heliosphere, and what roles do velocity shear, stream interactions, and proximity to the heliospheric current sheet play in that evolution?

evidence.quote: This section illustrates the issue with one complex problem that does appear to have been solved.
outward propagating Alfv?n waves are indicative of turbulence in the solar corona and the interaction of fast and slow wind does stir the solar wind and cause the turbulence to evolve.

artifact.status_search_result: Multiple recent observational and theoretical studies (Parker Solar Probe analyses, Helios–Voyager comparisons, and dedicated MHD turbulence studies) corroborate that outward-propagating Alfvénic fluctuations originate near the Sun and undergo radial dynamical evolution driven by velocity shear between fast and slow streams, stream interaction regions, and proximity to the heliospheric current sheet, where weakened radial magnetic field and transverse gradients reduce Alfvénicity. Shear-driven (Kelvin–Helmholtz-like) nonlinear couplings beyond the Alfvén critical zone are recognized as boosting low-frequency turbulence to observed heliospheric levels. The mechanism is regarded as essentially understood.

status_evidence.title: Influence of the heliospheric current sheet on the evolution of solar wind turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: Near the HCS, the Alfvénicity of the turbulence decreases ... due to weakening of radial magnetic field and transverse gradient in the background magnetic field.
status_evidence.claim: HCS proximity reduces Alfvénicity through identified MHD mechanisms.

status_evidence.title: Shear-driven Transition to Isotropically Turbulent Solar Wind Outside the Alfvén Critical Zone
status_evidence.snippet: Beyond the Alfvén critical zone ... energy in velocity contrasts drives nonlinear magnetized Kelvin–Helmholtz-like dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Velocity shear drives the transition from Alfvénic to isotropic turbulence.

status_evidence.title: Origin and evolution of fluctuations in the solar wind: Helios–Voyager comparisons
status_evidence.snippet: Outward propagating Alfvénic fluctuations are generated near the Sun and dynamical evolution involving shear-generated nonlinear couplings is important at all heliocentric distances.
status_evidence.claim: Long-standing observational confirmation of shear-driven evolution.

status_evidence.title: Sudden depletion of Alfvénic turbulence in rarefaction regions of CIRs at 1 AU
status_evidence.snippet: Stream interactions modulate the Alfvénic content of the turbulence.
status_evidence.claim: Stream interactions cause measurable depletion of Alfvénicity.
